title: Make the web shop quote what the ticket machine charges

blocks.text: A ferry operator sells tickets at a machine on the quay and, from next month, in a web shop. Finance owns the fares, and its rules are written as small step classes in `src/main/java/practice/Fares.java`: the base fare, a group discount, a peak surcharge. The ticket machine puts them together and has charged correctly for years.

Two things are wanted before the web shop opens. The web shop must quote exactly what the machine will charge for the same trip, or customers dispute the difference at the quay. And finance wants the group discount's threshold to change with the season, through the `FarePolicy` it is building: a machine and a web shop given a policy must both charge that policy's fares.
Finish the two `TODO`s, `FarePolicy.price(...)` and `WebShop.quote(...)`, and change anything else in the file you need to. About six lines in total.

cases.says: off-peak trips below and above the group threshold are quoted what the machine charges
a peak group whose base fare reaches the threshold gets the discount and the surcharge in both channels
a peak trip whose surcharge alone would cross the threshold is quoted the machine's price, without the discount
a fare policy built with another threshold sets the price at the machine and in the web shop

origin.section: Splitting by Verb Instead of by Actor Moves the Rule into Every Caller

concepts: Splitting one actor's rules into a class per step leaves the way the steps combine to each caller, so two callers can compute different results from correct steps; one class for the actor's steps gives every caller the same result.
